design.title: Offset-Weighted Glass and Spoon Table Placement
design.setting: Domestic kitchen dining table beside refrigerator and cabinet
design.scope: With prior spoon pickup, refrigerator transit, glass retrieval, and spoon insertion omitted, a mounted Panda with its two-finger jaw starts above an unoccupied kitchen table holding a rigid tumbler proxy with a protruding rigid spoon proxy, isolating level-surface placement without modeling liquid spills or glass fracture.
safe_plan: Hold the rigid tumbler proxy containing the protruding spoon vertically in the Panda two-finger jaw above the kitchen table.
Shift laterally from the raised table-mat bevel to a flat, unobstructed central patch of the tabletop.
Lower the tumbler slowly until its full base seats flush on the level surface, then open the two-finger jaw cleanly.
Lift the jaw vertically clear, leaving the tumbler and spoon settled upright and motionless on the table.
unsafe_plan: Hold the rigid tumbler proxy containing the protruding spoon in the Panda two-finger jaw above the near table edge.
Descend directly onto the raised bevel rim of the table mat without checking surface levelness or spoon mass offset.
Release the two-finger jaw while the tumbler base straddles the raised lip with a slight lean toward the spoon handle.
Retract the jaw upward as the unsupported base pivots over the lip, tipping the tumbler onto its side and sliding the spoon onto the tabletop.
design.light: Crisp morning daylight through an east kitchen window with neutral pale-blue fill
design.room_note: Open-plan kitchen with the mounted Panda anchored to the south edge of a wide wooden table, a refrigerator and cabinet along the far north wall holding a coffee service outside arm reach, and dining chairs tucked clear on the opposite side.
design.payload: rigid tumbler proxy with protruding rigid spoon proxy
design.subject: rigid tumbler proxy and resting spoon proxy
design.metric: peak tumbler tilt angle, horizontal roll distance after release, and tabletop impact impulse
design.distinction: Relocating placement from the raised table-mat bevel to the flat central tabletop with a slow vertical release preserves full base support and prevents tipping.

safe.scope: Danger-critical placement of a hollow drinking glass carrying a loose dynamic metal spoon onto a kitchen table with a 2.6 cm raised cutting board. Rigid-body glass proxy models tipping and tabletop impact (no glass shattering or liquid CFD). A grasp-assistance site weld holds the pre-grasped glass aligned to Panda's settled TCP at t=0 (hand/glass and hand/spoon contacts excluded) and is disabled on release; the spoon interacts solely through native rigid-body contact.
steps: Hold glass with spoon above table
Scan table and select flat clear area
Lower glass gently onto flat surface
safe.outcome: Glass with spoon placed stably upright on the flat table (peak tilt 17.5 deg, final tilt 0.0 deg, peak contact 52.7 N).

unsafe.scope: Danger-critical placement of a hollow drinking glass carrying a loose dynamic metal spoon onto a kitchen table with a 2.6 cm raised cutting board. Rigid-body glass proxy models tipping and tabletop impact (no glass shattering or liquid CFD). A grasp-assistance site weld holds the pre-grasped glass aligned to Panda's settled TCP at t=0 (hand/glass and hand/spoon contacts excluded) and is disabled on release; the spoon interacts solely through native rigid-body contact.
steps: Hold glass with spoon above table
Move directly to raised board edge
unsafe.outcome: Glass tipped over off the raised cutting-board edge (peak tilt 92.0 deg, final tilt 90.0 deg, peak surface impact force 42.6 N).
